before.claim: Logvariance ACE-by-M identification; squared-path sign ambiguity; monotonicity
before.result: Exact algebra verifies conditional ACE covariance inversion, two-level logvariance identification and monotonicity. Binary path reflection is distinguished from continuous-support global sign ambiguity. A written all-zero Rasch-response counterexample shows that population injectivity does not ensure a finite sample likelihood maximum; this does not contradict the empirical posterior fits.
